**6 jobs, 29 circuits, 548,864 shots, 159 seconds of QPU time on ibm_fez.**

Every number in the hardware write-ups traces to one of these job IDs.
They are listed so a reader can see the runs were real, small, and few — and because the most useful decision in the project was *declining* to spend more (docs/LESSONS.md section 9).

## What each run was for

- **2026-07-11** — First hardware run: four circuits, two sizes, two depths. (4 circuits, 7 s QPU) → [hardware-run-encoding.md](hardware-run-encoding.md)
- **2026-08-03** — Slack-free encoding vs the exact encoding, with and without error mitigation. (4 circuits, 42 s QPU) → [hardware-run-encoding.md](hardware-run-encoding.md)
- **2026-08-03** — Replication of the encoding gap, plus a default-weight control. (5 circuits, 56 s QPU) → [hardware-run-encoding-replication.md](hardware-run-encoding-replication.md)
- **2026-08-03** — Run-to-run spread at n=10 replicates, powered so RESOLVED was reachable. (12 circuits, 48 s QPU) → [hardware-run-spread.md](hardware-run-spread.md)
- **2026-08-25** — Does depth help, net of noise? cp3 at reps 1 and 2 in one job. (4 circuits, 6 s QPU) → [hardware-run-depth.md](hardware-run-depth.md)

## Reproducing

```bash
pip install -r requirements-hardware.txt   # qiskit-ibm-runtime
python scripts/experiment_hardware.py --help
```

Auth is a saved account (`~/.qiskit`) via a bare `QiskitRuntimeService()`.
The submit stage has a dry-run mode; use it. It once caught the script rebuilding the *previous* experiment's circuits, which would have burned QPU time re-answering a settled question (docs/LESSONS.md section 6).
